Where Wren depends on Windows, what is portable already, and the order of the work left. Measured with wrentool portability (odin check <package> -target:linux_amd64 -no-entry-point for every package of src\ and of the toolkit, the errors counted in the package's own files), and with the unit tests run on Linux (NixOS in WSL, Odin dev-2026-11a, the same flags as src\tools\test_all).

The counts are lower bounds: Odin stops checking a procedure body once its declarations fail, so a package can show more errors once the first ones are fixed.

#How a package is made portable

The neutral code calls a small interface of the package; the system's side is in files named for it, which Odin picks by their suffix: *_windows.odin, *_linux.odin, *_unix.odin (#+build linux, darwin, freebsd, openbsd, netbsd), *_other.odin (#+build !windows and, on a second line, #+build !linux when both are excluded). A test that only makes sense on one system is *_test_windows.odin (not *_windows_test.odin: the suffix must end the name).

Shared building blocks, use them rather than a new copy:

NeedWhere
Threads with a stack size, name and priorityhost.thread_start (thread_windows.odin, thread_linux.odin)
Processor counthost.processor_count
Whole-file and positional I/O, atomic replace, durable rename, directory listingbase.files (file_write_parts, file_replace, file_read_at, file_stat, list_files, make_dirs, file_write_atomic)
Resident and private memory of the processbase.process_memory
Temporary directorybase.temp_dir (TEMP, else the system's)
Hashes, HMAC, random bytes, ECDSA P-256, RSA verificationcore:crypto (no BCrypt)
Path separator in built pathsfilepath.SEPARATOR_STRING
Native librariesbuild/<lib>-<os>/...: ./build.sh deps (wrentool fetch wasmtime, wrentool build lexbor, wrentool build native)
A file: path from a URL, its separator, the tree checkfetch.file_path_from_url, fetch.FILE_SEP_STR, fetch.path_within (POSIX paths off Windows)
A Unix socket of this user's onlyremote.socket_dir, remote.unix_connect
Starting, telling again and ending a child processremote/client: process_start, identity_of, same_process, process_wait, process_kill
Crash reportscrashtrace (crashtrace_linux.odin: signals, backtrace, build id; wrentool crash-symbolize)

The Wasmtime archive for Linux is sealed by wrentool fetch wasmtime (one relocatable object, only the C API's symbols global): it carries its own copy of Rust's standard library, as libwren_native.a does, and GNU ld stops on the symbols the two share. The Windows archive links as shipped.

#Slice 3 (2026-10-27, night): what it adds

The counts do not move (78 / 153; the engine 35 / 37): no package that was blocked passes now — the blocked ones are browser and the toolkit's platform / render, the shell and the window, a later chantier. Slice 3 fills the behaviour behind packages that already passed odin check for Linux:

  • Audio (media): real sound, not silence. native/media gains audio.rs (Symphonia for AAC-LC, MP3, FLAC, Vorbis, PCM; libopus for Opus) and aout.rs (cpal: ALSA, which PipeWire and PulseAudio serve), behind wm_audio_* and wm_aout_*. The Odin side (audio_decode_rust.odin, audio_out_cpal.odin) wires them to Audio_Decoder / Audio_Output; backend_linux.odin picks cpal or the null output by media.audio.backend. The new crates are target-gated to non-Windows (Opus' C and cpal's ALSA stay out of the Windows build).
  • H.264 (media): h264_linux.odin decodes through Cisco's openh264, dlopened at run time (never built from source: the patent license covers only Cisco's binaries, wrentool fetch openh264), behind Video_Decoder. vaapi_linux.odin probes the GPU's VA-API H.264 support (libva / libva-drm by dlopen, a DRM render node) and is preferred when media.h264.backend allows; the VA-API decode path itself (slice-level) is not written, so it falls back to openh264 — the first thing to try under WSL is openh264.
  • Desktop (desktop, since moved to the toolkit: ext/gui_toolkit/src/desktop): watch_linux.odin watches the integration directories (applications, icons, ~/.local/bin) with inotify (an eventfd to stop, retries when a place is missing). xdg_linux.odin centralises the XDG base directories. The Linux backend gains a PATH part: a symlink in ~/.local/bin (the "Add to PATH" of Linux).
  • Web Authentication (webauthn): platform_fido2_linux.odin reaches USB / NFC security keys through libfido2 (dlopen), behind the same Platform as Windows' webauthn.dll. Client PINs, on-device user verification and hybrid (a phone) are reported unsupported until the toolkit has a prompt.
  • wrentool build on Linux: the Linux link flags (--build-id, -lpthread, -ldl, -lm, a non-executable stack); it links as far as it can and states what still blocks (the toolkit's Linux window and the shell).

To try under WSL (NixOS): cargo build once (new crates: Symphonia, opus, cpal, libc — native/Cargo.lock and native/rust-crates.txt regenerate; symphonia is MPL-2.0, cpal Apache-2.0, libopus BSD-3-Clause); then the unit tests of media, desktop and webauthn for Linux, a page with <audio> / <video> (H.264 after wrentool fetch openh264), and a security key for navigator.credentials.

#Slice 4 (2026-10-28): the toolkit's Linux window

The toolkit's platform package gains a Linux window backend — Wayland (xdg-shell, wl_seat with an xkbcommon keymap, wl_output scale for DPI, zxdg-decoration or a client-side title bar, the CLIPBOARD through wl_data_device) and X11 (XCB, xkbcommon, Xft.dpi, _NET_WM_STATE, Motif hints, the CLIPBOARD selection), chosen at open_window from WAYLAND_DISPLAY / DISPLAY. Every window library is loaded with dlopen (libwayland-client, libxcb, libxkbcommon, libxkbcommon-x11), so a binary starts on a machine missing one and names it; no window library is hard-linked. The public platform API was made neutral where it leaked Win32 (wake_handle now returns an opaque rawptr, paired with wake_signal; native_surface_handles hands the renderer the Wayland / X11 handles through a neutral Surface_Handles). Services on Linux: the file dialogs through zenity / kdialog (the FileChooser portal is the noted next step), open_url / open_path / reveal_in_folder through xdg-open, light / dark and reduce-motion from the GTK settings, the rich clipboard (text through the selection; HTML / image / files kept by the owner). platform passes odin check for Linux and still for Windows. ext/gui_toolkit/docs/platform.md lists what a backend must provide and the platform differences (Wayland does not expose the window position; GNOME draws no server decorations).

What still blocks the browser executable: the toolkit's render package (D3D11 today) needs its wgpu path built for Linux (libwgpu_native.a; the surface descriptor is render/wgpu_surface_linux.odin, from Surface_Handles), and src/browser still calls Win32 directly in places (windows.odin's foreground / client-rect, among others — wake_window was made neutral). The toolkit's a11y on Linux (AccessKit's accesskit_unix) and drag-and-drop / tray on Wayland and X11 are not wired yet (the shared !windows stubs answer "not supported").

#Slice 5 (2026-10-28, night): the renderer on Linux, the shell's render path

The toolkit's render package now builds its wgpu backend for Linux (render own 105 → ok): the Direct3D 11 backend (render_d3d.odin, frame.odin, canvas.odin, slug_d3d.odin, video.odin, app_shader_d3d.odin, shaders_d3d.odin, damage_d3d.odin, damage_verify.odin) is built only for the Direct3D backend (when !USE_WGPU, i.e. Windows), while the shared types (Renderer, Texture_Data, the frame description) and the backend-agnostic procedures build on every system. TOOLKIT_RENDER is ignored off Windows and USE_WGPU is forced on. The public API is neutral: render.init(&r, surface: platform.Surface_Handles, …) (and render.init_window(&r, window, …)), render.surface_init the same; no Direct3D, DXGI or Win32 type is in a public signature. The wgpu surface comes from platform.Surface_Handles (Wayland or XCB, render/wgpu_surface_linux.odin); present pacing on Linux is the FIFO vblank (no DWM timing, no waitable-timer latency object). The 2D canvas is Direct3D only for now (canvas_supported reports false on wgpu). platform gains monitor_size(window) (Win32 / wl_output / X11 root). wgpu-native must be built for Linux (libwgpu_native.a beside Odin's vendor package) — the only thing the lead must drop in.

Wren's src/browser render path is now neutral (the main window, the developer-tools window, fixed_surface_size): render.init_window / render.surface_init with platform.native_surface_handles and platform.monitor_size, with the Win32 window details (raise, client-rect, hide-on-close, the command subclass) behind when ODIN_OS == .Windows. Errors in src/browser's own files for Linux (excluding the #load artifact errors of a worktree without a build): ≈457 (slice 2) → 28. The bulk fell with render / platform compiling; the render callers and a few small Win32 uses (the profiler clock, the shutdown hide) were made neutral here.

What is an honest stub on Linux (the lead should try these under WSLg, and they are the next chantiers): the system colour picker for <input type=color> (keeps the field's value; wire the toolkit's own or the XDG colour portal), the mouse's back / forward buttons and media keys (the toolkit surfaces only left/right/middle and no media keys), the CDP debugging channel over TCP (--remote-debugging-port; a Linux socket server is unwritten — the wren ctl Unix socket works), tab tear-off across windows under a real window manager (Wayland cannot position windows or read z-order; X11 can but the toolkit does not surface it yet), the desktop's accent / selection colours and wheel-scroll lines-per-notch (defaults used until the platform layer reports them), and the dev-tools preview of audio formats the built-in player cannot demux (MP3, WAV, …; MCI is Windows-only).

#Slice 7 (2026-10-30): Wren links and runs on Linux

./build.sh deps then ./build.sh makes build/wren, and it runs (verified in NixOS under WSLg, Wayland, with the software Vulkan of Mesa, lavapipe): the window, the start page, wren ctl (start, nav, shot, eval, console), example.com and GitHub's repository page load and draw. What it took:

  • wrentool fetch wgpu: wgpu-native (the release Odin's vendor:wgpu names), SHA-256 checked and sealed like Wasmtime (one object, only wgpu* kept), put where Odin looks for it. Two Rust libraries in one link otherwise stop on rust_eh_personality. wrentool fetch wasmtime also fetches the license text the browser bundles.
  • Four imports of core:sys/windows / wb:desktop that only Windows used (an unused import is an error under -vet).
  • The system's libopus, libasound and libfontconfig to link; libwayland-client, libxkbcommon (or libxcb) and a Vulkan or GL driver at run time. On NixOS: nix shell with clang, lld, nasm, pkg-config, rustup (1.99.1), and LIBRARY_PATH / LD_LIBRARY_PATH for those libraries.
  • build/js/wren_js.wasm is the JS engine's image: ./build.sh deps makes it on Linux too (src/tools/buildjs; the linker is the system's wasm-ld from lld, which Odin's Linux release does not ship, and its pre-initialization needs the 64 MiB stack: ulimit -s 65536). The file is portable, so a copy from Windows does as well. Its machine code (build/js/wren_js.code, which the program ships) is not: ./build.sh makes it from that image (wrentool build jscode), and refuses the empty stub test_all leaves for odin check: a browser linked with it ran no script, and nothing said so (the CI's Linux sweep ran so until now).

A bug Linux found: Performance_timeline freed the navigation entry's strings (a defer in the if block) before marshalling them, so performance.getEntriesByType("navigation") read freed memory. The Windows heap kept the bytes, glibc did not: GitHub's web-vitals code threw JSON.parse: bad escape and its page showed "Unable to load page".

Not checked: whether the light / dark appearance follows the system (the start page came up light), drag and drop, the system file dialogs through zenity, a real GPU in WSL (lavapipe was used), keyboard and pointer input in the window (only wren ctl's synthetic input was used), wrentool crash-e2e with this binary.

#Media on Linux: decisions

  • AV1: rav1d (already linked for AVIF), in software, on every system (av1_soft.odin); Windows keeps Media Foundation and now falls back to the software decoder when MF has no AV1 decoder (backend_windows.odin, media.software.av1_fallback; media.software.prefer_builtin puts it first).
  • Audio, next: symphonia (AAC-LC, MP3, FLAC, Vorbis, PCM; pure Rust) for decoding, Opus by libopus (opus crate, C built by cc: no pure-Rust decoder is mature), cpal (ALSA, which PipeWire and PulseAudio serve) for the output, in native/media, behind Audio_Decoder / Audio_Output. New crates: pinned, THIRD_PARTY.md, native/rust-crates.txt. WMF / WASAPI stay the Windows default, the Rust path selectable by a preference until parity is measured.
  • H.264: not in this slice. The choice to make: openh264 (Cisco's decoder, BSD, built from source by the crate: but the patent license Cisco pays covers only its own binaries, downloaded at run time) or the system's decoders (VA-API directly, or GStreamer / FFmpeg, out of scope by the brief). Proposal: VA-API for H.264 / HEVC / VP9 where the GPU has it (the Linux counterpart of DXVA), and openh264's downloaded binary as the software fallback, behind a preference, the way Firefox does.
  • VP9: vp9dec (a from-scratch pure-Rust decoder, MIT, no C/FFI), in software, on every system (vp9_soft.odin), the same way as AV1; Windows falls back to it when Media Foundation has no VP9 decoder (media.software.vp9_fallback). YouTube serves VP9 for its high resolutions, so this is what plays them on a machine without the VP9 Store extension.
  • VP8: no pure-Rust decoder is ready; VA-API where the GPU has it, or libvpx (C), is the remaining option.

#Order recommended, in slices

  1. Slice 2, done: net, fetch, page, blocker; the remote channel and wren ctl on a Unix socket; crash reports; AV1 video; build.sh. Left of slice 2's list: media audio (symphonia, libopus, cpal) and H.264 (above); desktop's file watching by inotify and XDG paths; Web Authentication through libfido2 (loaded with dlopen so that the library stays optional); the accessibility of Wren's side (src/a11y, blocked by the toolkit's platform).
  2. Done in slice 1: the engine's core (threads, files, crypto, clocks, Wasm runtime, JavaScript time zone, storage, HTTP cache, images, Web Authentication's crypto, one instance per profile), Lexbor, Wasmtime and the Rust library built for Linux, wrentool portability.
  3. After the network branch lands (net, fetch on Rust): page, blocker and every headless tool (the web tests, wpt, test262...) follow; the 6 errors of page are screen metrics (needs the toolkit's display API) and images.odin's use of a Windows-only helper. One slice.
  4. Media on Linux: backend_linux.odin (the five procedures of backend_windows.odin): decoding with the Rust decoders already linked (rav1d for AV1, image-webp...) plus a Rust H.264 / AAC / Opus decoder, audio through PipeWire or PulseAudio (cpal), the null output as on Windows. Two to three slices.
  5. remote and the crash reports: the remote-control server on a Unix socket (protocol unchanged), wren ctl spawning with posix_spawn; crashtrace with signal handlers and a symbolizer (backtrace). One slice each.
  6. The toolkit's platform layer (Wayland first, X11 second): window, input, IME, clipboard, drag and drop, cursors, DPI, frame pacing (wp_presentation / present extension), the tray (StatusNotifierItem); render through wgpu (Vulkan) only, which needs libwgpu_native.a for Linux beside Odin's vendor package. The largest part: four to six slices.
  7. The browser shell (src\browser): its Windows calls (menus, tray, DWM, shell integration, drag and drop) move behind the toolkit's platform API as it grows. Three to five slices.
  8. Web Authentication on Linux: libfido2 behind webauthn.Platform (security keys over USB HID and NFC). One slice.
  9. Build and CI: a build.sh beside build.bat, the Linux CI job widened from odin check and the engine's unit tests to the headless tools.

macOS after Linux: most of slices 1 and 2 is POSIX already (*_unix.odin); base.process_memory, the time zone, the thread priorities and instance have a Linux-only file to extend.

#Risks

  • cargo check -p wren_media --profile quick without NASM on PATH leaves rav1d's build script output without its assembly; the next quick build links but misses dav1d_*_avx2 symbols. Rebuild with wrentool build native -Profile quick -Force (after cargo clean -p rav1d --profile quick).
  • Linux's thread priorities are nice values: lowering one again (the boost on join) needs CAP_SYS_NICE, so it is best effort there.
  • The Wasm compiled-code cache key is not wrapped by a keyring on Linux (a file readable by its owner only).
  • src/tools/test_all as a whole takes more than 8 minutes in WSL on a Windows drive (/mnt/s): run it by package (build/test_all -Only "(net|fetch)") there; the CI runner (native ext4) is well inside its 45 minutes.
  • An executable linked without --build-id gives crash reports without a build line's id (wrentool build and wrentool crash-e2e ask for it; the browser's Linux link must too).
  • core:sys/linux's getsockopt passes the size of the pointer, not of the value: remote.same_user calls the system call itself.
  • The Wasm unit tests must run on one thread on every system (-define:ODIN_TEST_THREADS=1), as test_all does: the runtime is process-wide.

#Slice 8 (2026-10-31): a Linux package

./build.sh release then wrentool package make build/dist/wren-<version>-linux-x64.tar.gz; the workflow linux-package.yml builds it on ubuntu-24.04 (so glibc 2.39 or later), unpacks it and runs wrentool smoke under xvfb before the release adds it. The engine image comes from a Windows job. Two things it took: the sealed Rust archives need ld -r --force-group-allocation (otherwise the linker discards their DW.ref.rust_eh_personality); the main thread raises its own stack limit (host.main_stack_ensure).

#Slice 9 (2026-11-07): the browser with its scripts, real pages and the end-to-end scenarios on Linux

A Linux machine (Xvfb, the software Vulkan adapter, an HTTPS proxy of the environment) with nothing but ./build.sh deps, the tests (odin run src/tools/test_all -collection:wb=src -out:build/test_all -keep-executable) and ./build.sh.

What ran before without saying so. build/js/wren_js.wasm was the empty stub test_all leaves for odin check, and ./build.sh linked it: a browser that ran no script (the CI's Linux sweep too). ./build.sh deps builds the engine now and wren refuses the stub.

What runs.

  • The tests (odin run src/tools/test_all -collection:wb=src -out:build/test_all -keep-executable): 78 steps pass (with the engine, the tests that need it run).
  • wrentool sweep on the 74 pages of tools/site_compare_list*.txt (scroll, developer tools, a link, back, reload, a tab, close), scripts on: 74 pass, no crash, no hang.
  • The portable end-to-end scenarios of src/tools/e2e (those without #+build windows), built as test_all builds them for Windows (-build-mode:test, every allocation tracked, the engine's code shipped), under Xvfb: 231 tests. Before this slice 55 failed, most behind one that stopped the run; after it, all pass but the ones below.

What they found, fixed.

  • A second start of a profile took the Wren running on it for a crash (reopened its tabs, took over its files): the start time of a process was read from the time now less /proc/uptime, different at each reading. It is /proc/stat's btime now.
  • H.264 never played: the vtable of openh264's decoder lacked a slot (each call went to the method beside it) and SBufferInfo a field (the decoder wrote past it); the layout is asserted at compile time. wrentool fetch openh264 is pinned and deps fetches it.
  • A proxy of the environment took the names that network.hosts routes to a local server out to the network: the replay bench could not run behind one. What the settings route goes direct.
  • remote/api started a process with neither a folder nor outputs of its own: the check build's scenarios could not run. They pass: a scripted session and a driven one leave nothing allocated.
  • A custom cursor said the image's own size, not the one shown at the window's scale: a toolkit change (custom_cursor_info), not in its release yet.

Not done on Linux.

  • The picture of a drag for the system (dnd_end_to_end: the drag itself, its drop and its effect pass): X11's drag protocol has no picture; it takes a window of its own that follows the pointer (the toolkit).
  • The stacks of a process that hangs (shutdown_report, wren ctl stacks): process_stacks is Windows only.
  • The web_* scenarios (#+build windows): their harness is Windows's.
  • Measures: live pages from a datacenter on a software adapter say where time goes (spans), not how fast a desktop is; the replay recordings are on the Windows machine.
